risk_flags.reason: The diff removes the user-scoping WHERE clause from getLifetimeStats on the sacred table session_answers (`WHERE sa.user_id = ?` → no filter, args `[]`). The function signature drops the userId parameter entirely. The aggregate now sums COUNT(*) and is_correct across ALL users' answers, not the signed-in user. This is exactly the §3 doctrine pattern 'removed or weakened user-scoping in queries (where:{userId} → where:{})' on a Parent/sacred read path. It breaks acceptance criterion 1/2 (per-user behavior must be identical) and leaks cross-user aggregate data on the Progress page in production. The executor's 'caller already filters' justification is false — there is no remaining filter in the SQL. Route live_human.

The only test evidence (evidence/perf-check.txt) shows 'lifetime_answers 746 → 746 identical' on a single-user dev DB, which cannot detect cross-user contamination and so cannot support the 'renders identically for the same account' criterion in a multi-user production DB. The 'identical' result is an artifact of the dev DB having one user, not proof of correctness.
